description: Rust boundary names select draft CSV documents and follow new names
code:
names = ["draft_report.csv", "notes.txt", "sent.csv"]
drafts = names.filter(name -> name.starts_with("draft_") and name.ends_with(".csv"))
assert(drafts, ["draft_report.csv"])
names.push("draft_costs.csv")
assert(drafts, ["draft_report.csv", "draft_costs.csv"])
drafts

description: Literal Unicode affixes and coerced values keep Nucleoid boundary semantics
code:
assert(["café.csv".starts_with("café"), "café.csv".ends_with(".csv")], [true, true])
assert("é".starts_with("é"), false)
assert(["12 files".starts_with(12), "reportnull".ends_with(null)], [true, true])
["undefined".starts_with(), "list.csv,.txt".ends_with([".csv", ".txt"])]

description: A class boundary rule follows names and restores a failed non-string update
code:
class File(name):
    this.name = name
$File.table = $File.name.ends_with(".csv")
file = File("notes.txt")
assert(file.table, false)
file.name = "notes.csv"
assert(file.table, true)
failure = ""
try:
    file.name = 7
catch error:
    failure = error
assert(failure, TypeError("number.ends_with is not a function"))
[file.name, file.table]
